conclusion: A detailed actual-contract rulebook exists, but six retrospective SHFE EOD samples plus dated product rules cannot establish a historical return, drawdown, cost, fill or personal-use result. The 5% annualized hurdle remains untested.

supports: The CU, AU and RU unit, tick, listed-month, scheduled last-trading-day, base margin and base price-limit parameters in the rulebook.
The premise that SHFE can adjust risk controls, so base figures cannot be extrapolated as historic or broker-specific requirements.
does_not_support: A personal account or short-selling eligibility conclusion.
A session-specific broker margin, commission, limit, fee, delivery cutoff or fill.
A return, drawdown, capacity or 5% annualized result.

actual_contract_eod_route.schema_note: TURNOVER is present in the 2022, 2024 and 2026 samples but absent in the retained 2016, 2018 and 2020 schema; absence is not treated as zero.
supports: The public official route currently returns identified actual contract rows rather than a preconstructed continuous series.
A future data room could use these fields as inputs to an actual-contract settlement ledger.
does_not_support: Complete coverage of every trading date and every listed/expired contract.
What data or contract lifecycle state was available on original decision dates.
Historical risk-control, broker, fee, quote, fill, delivery or account state.
A valid return test or trade.
The 65-session same-contract signal history required by the rulebook.
Account access, broker margin/fee, live bid/ask, capacity or a fill.

blocking_requirements.missing: A hash-bound every-session archive for all CU, AU and RU listed and expired contracts, with the same source fields and original identifiers.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: Six retrospectively fetched dates cannot construct the complete endpoint population, signal history, roll ledger, drawdown or annual-return test.

blocking_requirements.missing: Listing, expiry, exchange-adjusted last-trading dates, holiday/exception calendar, suspension and delivery-status history per contract/session.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: The rule selects actual contracts and enforces a delivery firewall. A generic 15th-day convention cannot prove which contracts were eligible at each historical decision.

blocking_requirements.requirement: Effective-session margin, limit, position and fee records
blocking_requirements.missing: Historical exchange notices and parameters, plus the actual broker add-on margin and commission/fee schedule for the route.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: Current base rules explicitly permit adjustments. Using base figures through history would misstate risk and could turn an infeasible position into a false fill.

blocking_requirements.missing: Historical bid/ask, limit-lock, depth/capacity, rejected/partial-fill states and a predeclared no-fill convention.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: A settlement-only curve cannot prove that a limit order, a stop or a two-leg roll would have filled.

blocking_requirements.missing: A separate confirmation from a licensed futures company of the person's ordinary-commodity contract access, short-side permission, fees, margin, delivery/force-close cutoff and applicable suitability steps.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: Exchange rule text never proves an individual account is eligible or configured to trade. No personal information is requested or retained in this case.

blocking_requirements.requirement: Pre-result frozen protocol and independent audit
blocking_requirements.missing: A signed rule version, data dictionary, source-cutoff record, unitized ledger, full rolling five-year endpoint policy, and a maker-checker audit before any performance result is read.
blocking_requirements.why_blocking: The current rulebook was written after public observations in this case. A positive replay now would be exploratory, not independent confirmation.

steps: Obtain a lawful, retained full actual-contract data package with documented rights and source timestamps; do not use an anonymous continuous series as a substitute.
Freeze a dated contract/corporate-event-style master covering listings, expiry, holiday adjustments, delivery and trading status for every candidate contract.
Archive effective exchange margin/limit/fee notices plus broker route schedules and an explicit conservative no-fill/partial-fill convention.
Confirm account-specific commodity-futures access externally without placing personal data in the research workspace.
Freeze this rulebook, a unitized marked-to-market ledger, actual close/open rolls, cost policy, risk-event logic and endpoint population before calculating any P&L.
Have an independent reviewer test source coverage, selections, each roll, margin changes, no-fill cases, return arithmetic and the full drawdown/endpoint population.
prohibitions: No historical performance calculation from a continuous series.
No return, 5% stability, position, allocation, holding or order claim before the blockers are closed.
No assumption that a failure to fill, a limit lock or a margin change is harmless.

distinctness.versus_R5: R5 used a public ETF accumulated-NAV proxy with monthly signal/rebalance logic and has already falsified a stable-year hurdle. C9 begins from SHFE actual CU, AU and RU contract identifiers, a same-contract signal, explicit close/open rolls and delivery firewalls. C9 has no return result and cannot rehabilitate R5.
distinctness.versus_H2: H2 examined CFFEX 10-year Treasury futures and could not validate a dated official actual-contract route. C9 uses three SHFE commodity families, retains current SHFE product/risk rules and six actual-contract daily-file samples. That stronger route is still not a complete historical or personal execution proof.

warnings: Source samples are retrospective; they do not prove original-date availability or revision state.
No private/paid data entitlement, broker data or personal account evidence is held.
